subject.title: [Bug]: Telegram provider intermittently stalls despite stable direct Bot API connectivity

question: Should this Telegram stall be resolved primarily as a shared proxy-agent scheme fix, an address-family/DNS policy change, or held for more live SOCKS5 reproduction first?
rationale: The source and Undici contract make a proxy-scheme bug plausible, but the available fixes touch compatibility-sensitive transport, DNS, fallback, or operator-policy surfaces and the open candidate PR is not yet proof-positive.

options.title: Prioritize Shared Proxy Fix
options.body: Treat the SOCKS/HTTP/HTTPS proxy helper contract as the canonical fix path, require explicit and env route tests, and keep DNS/IPv4 overrides as separate mitigations.

options.title: Prefer Address-Family Mitigation
options.body: Accept an opt-in force-IPv4 or DNS policy surface first, while leaving SOCKS scheme handling to a separate proxy issue or PR.

options.title: Hold For Live Repro
options.body: Keep the issue open but defer code direction until a redacted current-main SOCKS5 getMe/sendMessage reproduction is available.

recommendation.title: Prioritize Shared Proxy Fix
recommendation.body: Treat the SOCKS/HTTP/HTTPS proxy helper contract as the canonical fix path, require explicit and env route tests, and keep DNS/IPv4 overrides as separate mitigations.

likelyOwner.reason: They are listed for the Telegram subsystem and authored central fallback-chain work in the affected transport path.
